binders: t is an arbitrary real number.
conclusions: The real-valued measure, under gaussianReal 0 1, of the set of real x satisfying |x| >= t is at most 2 * exp(-(t^2)/2).
mathematical_definitions: The event is {x in Real | |x| >= t}, with |x| = max(x, -x).
Measure.real(mu, s) is the real number obtained by applying toReal to the measure value mu(s).
The right-hand side is 2 e^{-t^2/2}, using ordinary real multiplication, division, negation, squaring, and exponential.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonnegative real number t, the real-valued gaussianReal(0, 1) measure of the two-sided tail event consisting of real x with |x| at least t is no greater than 2 e^{-t^2/2}.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The conclusion is required only when t >= 0; for negative t the implication has a false premise and is therefore vacuous.
The threshold event uses the inclusive comparison |x| >= t, not a strict inequality.

The event measure is passed through toReal before comparison. The dossier does not supply the behavior of toReal on an infinite measure value, although the named Gaussian construction is intended to be finite.
The statement directly bounds a measure of a subset of Real; it does not quantify a random variable or explicitly assert normalization, independence, moments, or any other distributional properties.
The statement provides only this upper bound; it asserts neither a matching lower bound nor optimality of the constant or exponent.
ambiguities: The dossier does not define gaussianPDF, volume.withDensity, or the precise conventional interpretation of gaussianReal's second parameter v, so it does not by itself establish whether v denotes variance, standard deviation, or another Gaussian scale parameter. The exact object is nevertheless unambiguous as gaussianReal 0 1 with its displayed branch definition.
The dossier defines Measure.real through toReal but does not include the definition of toReal; its exceptional behavior, if any, cannot be reconstructed solely from the supplied dependency meanings.
